title: A/B Test Campaign Performance Leaderboard
prompt: Your fashion ecommerce site runs weekly A/B test campaigns pairing two marketing strategies head-to-head. Each campaign record shows which two strategies competed (strategy_a and strategy_b) and how many conversions each achieved (conversions_a and conversions_b). A strategy earns 3 points for a win (more conversions), 1 point for a draw (equal conversions), and 0 for a loss. Write a query that produces a leaderboard showing every strategy (including those that have never been tested) with their total points and total campaigns played. The output columns must be strategy_name, total_points, campaigns_played. Order the results by total_points descending, then by strategy_name ascending. Strategies with no campaigns should appear with 0 points and 0 campaigns.
schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE strategies (strategy_id INT PRIMARY KEY, strategy_name VARCHAR(100)); CREATE TABLE ab_campaigns (campaign_id INT PRIMARY KEY, strategy_a INT, strategy_b INT, conversions_a INT, conversions_b INT, week_start DATE, FOREIGN KEY (strategy_a) REFERENCES strategies(strategy_id), FOREIGN KEY (strategy_b) REFERENCES strategies(strategy_id));
example_input_data: INSERT INTO strategies (strategy_id, strategy_name) VALUES (1, 'Email Blast'), (2, 'Instagram Story'), (3, 'Facebook Retarget'), (4, 'Influencer Collab'), (5, 'Google Shopping'); INSERT INTO ab_campaigns (campaign_id, strategy_a, strategy_b, conversions_a, conversions_b, week_start) VALUES (101, 1, 2, 45, 38, '2024-01-08'), (102, 2, 3, 52, 52, '2024-01-15'), (103, 1, 3, 60, 41, '2024-01-22'), (104, 4, 2, 33, 29, '2024-01-29'), (105, 3, 1, 47, 50, '2024-02-05'), (106, 4, 3, 28, 35, '2024-02-12');

composite_moves: unpivot both sides of each campaign via UNION ALL: one branch for strategy_a with (strategy_a, conversions_a, conversions_b), second branch for strategy_b with (strategy_b, conversions_b, conversions_a)
per-row CASE to score each side: WHEN own > opp THEN 3, WHEN own = opp THEN 1, ELSE 0
GROUP BY strategy_id and SUM points, COUNT campaigns
LEFT JOIN from strategies dimension table to ensure every strategy appears, COALESCE nulls to 0

hints: Each campaign row represents two participants; you need to examine each strategy's performance separately.
Use UNION ALL to create one row per strategy per campaign, carrying both its own conversions and its opponent's conversions, then apply a point formula based on the comparison.

After scoring each strategy's individual campaign results, group by strategy and sum the points. To include strategies with zero campaigns, start from the strategies table and LEFT JOIN your aggregated results, using COALESCE to fill NULLs with 0.
answer_key:
WITH campaign_splits AS (
  SELECT strategy_a AS strategy_id, conversions_a AS own, conversions_b AS opp
  FROM ab_campaigns
  UNION ALL
  SELECT strategy_b, conversions_b, conversions_a
  FROM ab_campaigns
),
scored AS (
  SELECT
    strategy_id,
    CASE
      WHEN own > opp THEN 3
      WHEN own = opp THEN 1
      ELSE 0
    END AS points
  FROM campaign_splits
),
aggregated AS (
  SELECT
    strategy_id,
    SUM(points) AS total_points,
    COUNT(*) AS campaigns_played
  FROM scored
  GROUP BY strategy_id
)
SELECT
  s.strategy_name,
  COALESCE(a.total_points, 0)::TEXT AS total_points,
  COALESCE(a.campaigns_played, 0)::TEXT AS campaigns_played
FROM strategies s
LEFT JOIN aggregated a ON s.strategy_id = a.strategy_id
ORDER BY COALESCE(a.total_points, 0) DESC, s.strategy_name ASC;

_meta.scenario: a fashion ecommerce site tracking add-to-cart and conversion
